plan_item: Stage 17 / callback runtime and durable incident resume
intent: Wire reviewed callback keys into the runtime without exposing secret material, authenticate external incident callbacks at the application boundary, and resume the exact durable ADGO incident wait/human node without granting callback credentials authority over any other execution or action.
invariants: Callback runtime is disabled by default and application startup fails closed when enabled configuration, key references, key material or replay policy are invalid.
Secret values never enter runtime JSON, logs, audit details or HTTP responses; only secret references and key IDs are configuration data.
A callback can target only the execution, node, event and action bound into its signed claims.
Medium-risk owner acknowledgement uses the durable ADGO inbox event ID and therefore remains deduplicated across redelivery and process restart.
High-risk owner decisions can resolve only the configured incident human node; a stale or already-resolved node cannot execute a second semantic transition.
Callback authentication is bearer-token based and independent of cookie sessions/CSRF; callback credentials are never forwarded to downstream integrations.
Every accepted or rejected callback decision produces an audit record without recording the bearer token or signing key material.
contracts: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md security authority and orchestration boundaries
acceptance_evidence: Disabled-by-default and malformed-enabled callback configuration tests pass.
Secret-reference resolution and key-rotation overlap tests pass without exposing key bytes.
Binding mismatch, tampered bearer, expired token and unknown-key requests fail closed and are audited.
Concurrent duplicate callback delivery changes one durable incident execution at most once.
Restart/redelivery tests prove medium-risk event dedupe and high-risk stale-resolution safety.
Packet-wide critical mutation testing has no LIVED, NOT COVERED or TIMED OUT blockers.
Repository CI, race and supply-chain/security qualification remain green.
